name: University of Copenhagen
about: All University of Copenhagen bachelor’s degrees are taught in Danish. If you can meet its academic Danish requirement, an IB Diploma can be assessed in either admissions quota. If you need an English-taught bachelor’s degree, look at other institutions; UCPH offers English-taught options at master’s level.

languageOfInstruction.note: UCPH requires academic Danish for every bachelor’s degree. There are no fully English-taught bachelor’s programmes.

notes: Apply on optagelse.dk by 15 March at 12:00 Danish time with the documents already available. Normally you must meet and document entry requirements by 5 July at 12:00. If your final school diploma is issued late, check UCPH’s exception before applying: your school may need to provide a letter with the March application.

Starting university straight after your IB exams? Give your IB coordinator permission before 1 May to share your results electronically with UCPH. The university’s IB institution code is 002600. This is separate from the March application.

IB Diploma applicants can be assessed in both quotas. Quota 1 ranks by the converted Danish grade average. The usual minimum is 6.0 (Musicology is exempt; dispensations are limited). Meeting the minimum does not guarantee an offer. Quota 2 uses a test and an interview for shortlisted applicants. Programme-specific subject and language requirements still apply. Check the IB guidance before relying on Course Results alone; an individual assessment is not automatic equivalence.

Check UCPH’s IB language criteria before choosing a Danish subject. Some SL and language B qualifications have extra conditions. If using Studieprøven instead, UCPH also requires evidence of passing your mother tongue at the highest upper-secondary level. The normal minimum is 2 in every part; Medicine in Copenhagen or Køge, Dentistry and Dental Hygiene require 7 in every part.
A, B and C in the Danish subject table are subject levels, not grades. The converted 6.0 is on the Danish 7-point scale.

UCPH generally charges tuition to citizens outside the EU/EEA and Nordic countries unless their residence status qualifies for an exemption. Check the university’s fee guidance for your circumstances; no bachelor programme rate is stated here.
